LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 1.1.1 ATTENTIVE LISTENING: POETRY

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.1: Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Attentive Listening: Poetry
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Attentive Listening: Poetry, part of Strand 1 in Grade 5 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: What should you do in order to listen attentively?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. identify names of clothes and attire (nouns) in the community from an oral text,

2. work collaboratively to construct sentences using the nouns identified,

3. brainstorm on various features of a poem with peers,

4. recite poems based on the theme with expressions (non-verbal cues),

5. work with peers to paraphrase the poem in their own words without altering the ideas,

6. listen attentively to recorded clips of simple poems on cultural attire and answer comprehension questions,

7. team up with peers to compose a spoken-word poetry item on the theme.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. identify names of clothes and attire (nouns) in the community from an oral text,
2. work collaboratively to construct sentences using the nouns identified,
3. brainstorm on various features of a poem with peers,
4. recite poems based on the theme with expressions (non-verbal cues),
5. work with peers to paraphrase the poem in their own words without altering the ideas,
6. listen attentively to recorded clips of simple poems on cultural attire and answer comprehension questions,
7. team up with peers to compose a spoken-word poetry item on the theme.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Attentive Listening: Poetry together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: This is developed as the learner engages actively using facts and examples when

brainstorming various features of a poem.

• Creativity and Imagination: This is enhanced as the learner exchanges new ideas that inspire creative thinking when reciting

poems on cultural attire using non-verbal cues.

Values:
• Peace: This is achieved as the learner displays tolerance while working collaboratively with peers to construct sentences

using nouns.

• Unity: This is developed as the learner works harmoniously with peers to paraphrase the poems in their own words without

altering ideas.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Cultural awareness: This is promoted as the learner identifies cultural attires and clothing in various communities in their

neighbourhood.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the concept on attentive listening skills to their learning and use of similar skills in English language.
